Theme 060 · Signature directions

Neo-Brutalist

Neo-brutalism, braked for a serious product: off-white paper on a 72 px grid, 5 px ink outlines, hard unblurred offset shadows, flat fills, taped cards, rotated stickers, starbursts and one scrolling ticker. Everything moves in steps and every press lands on a beat — loud, but never messy: numbers and tables are never tilted.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The lockup card drops and presses, tape sticks on the off-beats, tagline blocks slide in from opposite sides, and the CTA slams up from below into its 14 px shadow on the sting; the cursor clicks and the button depresses for 120 ms.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Heavy card — 5 px ink outline + 9 px hard offset shadow, no blur, r14
  • Press — card translates into its own shadow in 80–120 ms, always on a beat
  • Block headline — Manrope 800 uppercase on flat fills (white, amber, teal, soft teal, coral)
  • Sticker + starburst — rotated 2–8°, slapped on with 1.3 → 1 + wobble; starbursts only for errors and one stat
  • Tape — soft-teal strips with dashed edges holding cards to the page
  • Ticker strip — the only continuously moving element: a coral/ink band scrolling left

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Slam-in — y −120 → 0 on steps(3) at 12 fps, 0.25 s, landing on the beat; no easing curves
  • Press — translate(9 px, 9 px) + shadow 9 → 0 in 0.1 s, then back in 0.1 s — the “click” on every downbeat (every 2 s at 120 BPM)
  • Ticker — linear x scroll at 1 bar per 480 px (240 px/s) for the whole scene — the constant against the stepped hits

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

It is instantly recognisable and survives any feed — nobody scrolls past a hard shadow. Risk: playful styles can undercut trust for a data product, and contrast/clutter get out of hand fast; keep the 72 px grid rigid, max three fills per frame, coral only for errors and the CTA.

Adapt to your product: Turn your product’s key objects into heavy cards and let the one that needs attention pop out with a starburst; your CTA is simply the heaviest card in the film.

References: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/neobrutalism/ (NN/G: neobrutalism definition and usability cautions) · https://www.figma.com/blog/config-2024-branding/ (Config 2024 identity: shapes and motion principles (shift, transform))
